stories.topic: EURO AREA / ECB / SPAIN / FRANCE / GERMANY / EUR / POLICY
stories.headline: Euro-area countries select De Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
stories.body: Reuters reported that euro-area countries selected Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president. They also nominated Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for the executive board, with market operations and chief economist roles expected respectively. The candidates still face a confirmation process, with a final decision expected at the December summit. Political selection is distinct from completed formal appointment and from an interest-rate decision.
stories.analysis: Leadership continuity is an expectation; the ECB’s collective decision process and inflation outlook still govern monetary policy.
stories.watch_next: The December confirmation process and monetary-policy decision.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 covered prospective French, German and Spanish appointments; v2 added Dutch backing and the expected nomination process. This v3 adds political selection and the two board nominations. The producer’s De Cos alias v2 maps to this established leadership event’s v3; earlier versions remain intact.

stories.topic: US / UK / ALTRIA / MO / IMPERIAL BRANDS / IMB / MERGERS AND ACQUISITIONS
stories.headline: Altria considers a possible cash offer for Imperial Brands
stories.body: Reuters reported that Altria was considering a possible all-cash offer for Imperial Brands and discussing a potential transaction involving part of Imperial’s business with another party. Imperial said it had received no approach or proposal. Reuters’s European closing report put Imperial’s session gain at 13.3%; that closing return is separate from its larger intraday rise and is not an offer price. Under UK takeover rules, Altria’s stated deadline to announce a firm offer or withdraw is 24 December 2026, subject to applicable extensions. No completed acquisition or confirmed financing was established.
stories.analysis: A potential acquisition raises leverage and capital-allocation questions, but its terms and funding remain unconfirmed.
stories.watch_next: A formal proposal, financing terms and the 24 December deadline.

stories.topic: KAZAKHSTAN / RUSSIA / ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / NVIDIA / NVDA / EXPORT CONTROLS
stories.headline: Kazakhstan advances AI cooperation with Russia
stories.body: Reuters reported that Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed Russian technology companies at an AI conference in Moscow. The report connected this cooperation with Kazakhstan’s earlier AI plans and a previously announced Nvidia chip order. Freedom Holding’s US$2 billion Sovereign AI Hub plan dates to October; it is background rather than new investment committed during this report window. The reporting does not establish a new shipment, completed transaction or sanctions breach.
stories.analysis: Cross-border infrastructure plans warrant attention to export permissions, counterparties and actual project delivery.
stories.watch_next: Verified export permissions, company confirmations and project milestones.
